This directory is reserved for your frontend application (e.g., React, Next.js, Vite, Vue, Angular).

"# Fullstack Application

## Project Structure

```
├── client/                     # Frontend client workspace
└── server/                     # Backend Express + TypeScript server
    ├── src/
    │   ├── controllers/        # Request handling and response logic (MVC)
    │   │   └── dummy.controller.ts
    │   ├── models/             # Data structure and business logic (MVC)
    │   │   └── dummy.model.ts
    │   ├── routes/             # Route definitions and handlers
    │   │   ├── dummy.routes.ts
    │   │   └── index.ts
    │   ├── app.ts              # Express application setup
    │   └── index.ts            # Server entry point
    ├── .env                    # Environment variables
    ├── .env.example
    ├── package.json
    └── tsconfig.json
```

## Running the Server

1. Navigate to the `server` folder:
   ```bash
   cd server
   ```

2. Install dependencies (if not already installed):
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

3. Start in development mode (hot-reload):
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

4. Build and run in production:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm start
   ```

## API Endpoints

- **GET `/`**: Base health check (`{ "message": "Server is up and running!" }`)
- **GET `/api/health`**: API health check status
- **GET `/api/dummy`**: Returns dummy items from the MVC model layer
- **POST `/api/dummy`**: Creates a dummy item (`{ "name": "...", "message": "..." }`)
"

"# Decision Log & Architecture Notes

This document records key technical decisions, architectural choices, and rationales for the project.

---

## Decision Record 001: Project Directory Structure

- **Date:** 2026-11-27
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:**
  The project requires a fullstack foundation separating server-side logic from frontend client development.
- **Decision:**
  - Create two top-level directories: `server` and `client`.
  - Dedicate `server` to the Express backend and `client` to the frontend app (e.g., React/Vite/Next.js).
  - Add `ai_logs/` to track AI interactions, prompt contexts, and audit logs.
  - Document all architectural choices in `NOTES.md`.

---

## Decision Record 002: Backend Architecture & Technology Stack

- **Date:** 2026-11-27
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:**
  The backend needs to be robust, maintainable, type-safe, and follow clean design patterns without unnecessary template rendering overhead.
- **Decision:**
  - **Runtime & Language:** Node.js with TypeScript (`tsc` for typechecking/builds and `tsx` for fast dev hot-reloading).
  - **Framework:** Express 4.x with `cors` and `dotenv`.
  - **Pattern:** MVC (Model-View-Controller) architecture tailored for API backends:
    - **Models (`src/models`):** Define data contracts, entity schemas, and data access logic.
    - **Controllers (`src/controllers`):** Handle HTTP requests, input validation, and response formatting.
    - **Routes (`src/routes`):** Define route endpoints and delegate actions to controllers.
    - **No Views Folder:** Since this is a REST API server providing JSON data to a decoupled client, the server does not render HTML templates.
  - **Entry Points:**
    - `src/app.ts`: Decoupled Express app setup (useful for unit/integration testing without binding ports).
    - `src/index.ts`: Server startup script binding to `process.env.PORT`.

---

=== BRIEF.md ===
# Switchboard — build round

Build the first version of **Switchboard**, a shared team inbox. Customers
write to a business over a messaging provider. Support agents (people who work
at that business) log in, see conversations arrive in real time, reply, and
leave private notes for each other.

Several businesses (workspaces) use the same deployment. They must never see
each other's data.

**You will not finish everything below.** That is intended. Build the product
first, then make it survive: a small product that keeps working when the
network is bad, the process dies or a second copy is started beats a large one
that works only on the happy path.

Use any AI tools you like. You own every line you submit: in the follow-up
call we open your code, ask why it is the way it is, and debug it with you.

## The two hours

| Time | What |
| --- | --- |
| 0:00 – 0:10 | Read `START_HERE.md` and this brief. Start the services. |
| 0:10 – 1:50 | Build. Commit at least every 15 minutes. |
| 1:50 – 2:00 | Run the full check, push, make the repository public, send the form. See `SUBMISSION.md`. |

The form closes at 2:00. What counts is the commit you name in the form.

## How it fits together

```
simulated customers -> Pigeon :4010 --webhook POST--> YOUR SERVER --WebSocket--> YOUR REACT APP
        (given)          (given)                      (you build)                 (you build)

agent types a reply -> YOUR SERVER -> POST /v1/messages on Pigeon -> status webhooks back to you
```

You build the business side only. The customers are simulated and live inside
Pigeon; there is no customer app, and they do not answer your replies.

| Service | Port | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pigeon | 4010 | The messaging provider (simulated). Sends you webhooks, accepts your sends. Unreliable on purpose. See `PIGEON.md`. |
| Mock IdP | 4020 | OpenID Connect provider with five test users. Discovery at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Client id `switchboard-web`. PKCE (S256) is required. |
| MongoDB | 27017 | Real. |
| Redis | 6379 | Real. |
| Elasticsearch | 9200 | Real, optional: `npm run up:search`. |
| Paybox | 4030 | Simulated payment provider. Only for the bonus. See `PAYBOX.md`. |

`scaffold/` is an optional empty shell (Express + TypeScript server, Vite +
React app, already pointed at the services). It has no product code. Use it,
or delete it and bring your own Node stack; then change the `start` command in
`switchboard.json`.

## What to build

### The product
1. **Login.** Sign in through the IdP (authorization code + PKCE). A user's
   workspaces and roles come from the `workspaces` claim. Roles: `admin`, `agent`.

args.Content:
"# Switchboard Decision Log & Technical Notes

This document records the architectural and technical decisions made for the Switchboard application build.

---

## Decision Record 001: Project Architecture & Environment

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:**
  The project is **Switchboard**, a shared team inbox where simulated customers message over Pigeon, and human support agents manage conversations across multiple isolated business workspaces.
- **Decision:**
  - Standardize on the official `scaffold/` layout:
    - `scaffold/server`: Express + TypeScript backend listening on `process.env.PORT` with MongoDB and Redis.
    - `scaffold/web`: Vite + React frontend for support agents.
  - Retain the test harness (`harness/`), mock identity provider (`idp/`), and simulated Pigeon messaging provider (`pigeon/`).
  - Configure root `switchboard.json` pointing to `npm run scaffold:install` and `npm --prefix scaffold/server start`.

---

## Decision Record 002: Backend Libraries & Dependencies

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:**
  The backend must satisfy level checks 1 through 5:
  1. Pigeon Webhooks with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification over raw request body.
  2. IdP Authentication via OIDC and PKCE (S256).
  3. Real-time updates over WebSockets (`/ws?workspace=<id>`).
  4. Outbound replies with rate-limiting, idempotency, and outage recovery.
- **Decision:**
  - Added `ws` and `@types/ws` for real-time WebSocket connection handling.
  - Added `cors` and `@types/cors` for secure cross-origin communication with the Vite client (`http://localhost:5173`).
  - Added `cookie-parser` and `@types/cookie-parser` for reading session cookies across both HTTP APIs and WebSocket upgrade handshakes.
  - Added `jose` for lightweight OIDC token and claims verification.
  - Leveraged `mongodb` and `ioredis` for multi-tenant persistence and distributed state/locking.

---

## Decision Record 003: Version Control & Submission Compliance

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:**
  The repos
<truncated 251 bytes>

"# Switchboard Architecture & Decisions

See [NOTES.md](file:///c:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/goghl/starter/NOTES.md) for detailed architecture decision records.

### Summary
1. **Scaffold Layout:** Using `scaffold/server` and `scaffold/web`.
2. **Backend Tech Stack:** Node.js (Node 22+), Express, TypeScript (`tsx`), MongoDB, Redis (`ioredis`), WebSockets (`ws`), OIDC/PKCE (`jose`).
3. **Pigeon Integration:** Handling `message.inbound` and `message.status` webhooks with HMAC-SHA256 verification and replay protection.
4. **Tenant Isolation:** Workspace boundaries enforced on every query and WebSocket frame (`seq` integer ordering).
"

This directory contains records, session transcripts, and notes of AI-assisted engineering and architectural decisions during the build round.

Here is how to run the Switchboard stack on your local machine:

---

### Step 1: Start Supporting Services (Redis & Simulators)

Your system already has **Docker 29.9** and **MongoDB (port 27017)** running locally.

To spin up the remaining services (Redis, Pigeon messaging simulator, Mock IdP, and Paybox):

```powershell
docker compose up -d redis pigeon idp paybox
```

> [!NOTE]
> We start `redis`, `pigeon`, `idp`, and `paybox`. Since your local MongoDB is already running on port `27017`, this prevents any port conflict.

---

### Step 2: Verify Service Health

Run the diagnostic check from the repository root:

```powershell
npm run doctor
```

All ports (`27017`, `6379`, `4010`, `4020`, `4030`) should show **`PASS`**.

---

### Step 3: Start the Backend Server

Open your first terminal and run:

```powershell
npm run scaffold:server
```

- **URL:** [http://localhost:4000](http://localhost:4000)
- **Health Check:** [http://localhost:4000/healthz](http://localhost:4000/healthz)
- Features hot-reloading with `tsx watch`.

---

### Step 4: Start the Frontend App (Vite + React)

Open a second terminal and run:

```powershell
npm run scaffold:web
```

- **URL:** [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173)

---

### Useful Commands While Developing

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `npm run inbound` | Simulates a customer sending a message to your webhook immediately |
| `npm run quiet` | Stops the automatic customer message trickle so your logs stay clean |
| `npm run drizzle` | Resumes the automatic message trickle (1 message every 4–8s) |
| `npm run report` | Shows what Pigeon recorded of your webhook responses and sends |
| `npm run check` | Runs Level 1 test suite against your server (*stop your dev server before running*) |

"# Switchboard — Architecture & Key Decisions

## What We Built So Far
- **Project Structure (`scaffold/server` & `scaffold/web`):** Decoupled Express + TypeScript (ESM) backend and Vite + React frontend, sharing a single multi-tenant deployment (`ws_acme`, `ws_globex`) backed by MongoDB and Redis.
- **Pigeon Webhook Ingestion (`POST /webhooks/pigeon`):**
  - **Raw-Body Signature Verification (`src/signature.ts`):** Mounted `express.raw({ type: '*/*', limit: '1mb' })` exclusively on `/webhooks/pigeon` so HMAC-SHA256 is computed over the exact raw bytes received rather than re-serialized JSON. Uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after strict length and hex validation, and enforces a 5-minute replay tolerance (`toleranceSeconds = 300`) while allowing small future clock skew.
  - **Strict Defensive Status Mapping:** Returns `401` for missing/malformed/bad/expired signatures, `400` for unparseable JSON or missing envelope fields (`id`, `type`, `workspace`), `200` (ignore) for unknown event types or unknown workspaces, and `503` if MongoDB fails—never `5xx` on client errors and never `2xx` if storage fails.
  - **Crash-Safe Idempotent Storage (`src/store.ts`):** No in-memory deduplication state is used; all state lives in MongoDB so multiple server instances and crash/restart cycles behave identically. Unique indexes on `messages (workspace, messageId)` and `conversations (workspace, contact)` are awaited via `ensureIndexes()` before `server.listen()`.
  - **Two-Step Idempotent Pipeline:** Every delivery (including duplicates) inserts the message (treating Mongo duplicate-key `11000` as success) and then upserts the conversation using `$setOnInsert` (for `status`, `assignee`, `createdAt`) and `$max` (for `lastActivityAt`) so out-of-order events never move activity backwards and crashes between steps self-heal on Pigeon retry.

## What Is Deferred / Next
- `message.status` webhook handling (stubbed with `200` + `TODO`) will be wired into the outbound reply pipeline.

6:   - **Raw-Body Signature Verification (`src/signature.ts`):** Mounted `express.raw({ type: '*/*', limit: '1mb' })` exclusively on `/webhooks/pigeon` so HMAC-SHA256 is computed over the exact raw bytes received rather than re-serialized JSON. Uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after strict length and hex validation, and enforces a 5-minute replay tolerance (`toleranceSeconds = 300`) while allowing small future clock skew.
7:   - **Strict Defensive Status Mapping:** Returns `401` for missing/malformed/bad/expired signatures, `400` for unparseable JSON or missing envelope fields (`id`, `type`, `workspace`), `200` (ignore) for unknown event types or unknown workspaces, and `503` if MongoDB fails—never `5xx` on client errors and never `2xx` if storage fails.
8:   - **Crash-Safe Idempotent Storage (`src/store.ts`):** No in-memory deduplication state is used; all state lives in MongoDB so multiple server instances and crash/restart cycles behave identically. Unique indexes on `messages (workspace, messageId)` and `conversations (workspace, contact)` are awaited via `ensureIndexes()` before `server.listen()`.
9:   - **Two-Step Idempotent Pipeline:** Every delivery (including duplicates) inserts the message (treating Mongo duplicate-key `11000` as success) and then upserts the conversation using `$setOnInsert` (for `status`, `assignee`, `createdAt`) and `$max` (for `lastActivityAt`) so out-of-order events never move activity backwards and crashes between steps self-heal on Pigeon retry.

   - **Outbox Worker & Pigeon Rate Limiting** ([outbox.ts](file:///c:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/goghl/my-app/scaffold/server/src/outbox.ts), [status.ts](file:///c:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/goghl/my-app/scaffold/server/src/status.ts)): Created a distributed Lua-based token bucket (capacity 7, 3.5 tokens/sec refill), atomic lease-based worker queue (`leaseMs=20000`), Retry-After handling with Redis cooldown keys (`sb:cool:<workspace>`), and forward-only status progression (`queued` < `sent` < `delivered` = `failed`).
   - **Grader Harness Endpoints** ([grader.ts](file:///c:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/goghl/my-app/scaffold/server/src/routes/grader.ts)): Mounted isolated `/__grader/` endpoints (`/reset`, `/snapshot`, `/reply`, `/claim`) with `x-grader-token` verification.

"# Switchboard

A multi-tenant, reliable shared customer support inbox built for harsh real-world network conditions (delayed/dropped requests, replayed events, hostile providers, and sudden process terminations).

---

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js**: >= 22.0.0 (Node 22 or 24 recommended)
- **Docker & Docker Compose**: For local infrastructure services (MongoDB, Redis, Pigeon messaging simulator, Mock IdP, Paybox)
- **Git** with Bash / `sh` available in `PATH`

---

## Quick Start (Clean Clone)

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Ishaqznz/my-switchboard.git
cd my-switchboard
```

### 2. Environment Configuration

Copy the example environment configuration into `.env` (the defaults work out-of-the-box with the local Docker containers and test harness):

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

### 3. Start Infrastructure Dependencies

Start the required backing services (MongoDB, Redis, Pigeon messaging simulator, Mock IdP, Paybox):

```bash
npm run up
```

Verify that all dependencies and ports are ready:

```bash
npm run doctor
```

> **Without Docker?** You can run `npm run mocks` with standard Node.js and point `MONGO_URL` and `REDIS_URL` in `.env` to your local MongoDB and Redis instances.

### 4. Install Dependencies

Install dependencies for both backend and frontend:

```bash
npm run scaffold:install
```

---

## Running in Development

### Start the Server (Backend)

The server runs Express with TypeScript (ESM, NodeNext) using `tsx`:

```bash
npm run scaffold:server
```
Server listens on `http://localhost:4000` (or the port specified by `$PORT`).

### Start the Web Application (Frontend)

```bash
npm run scaffold:web
```
Frontend runs with Vite on `http://localhost:5173`.

---

## Running the Automated Test Harness & Grader Checks

> **Important:** Stop your local dev server (`Ctrl+C`) before running any checks. The test harness launches and manages isolated server instances on custom ports behind an i
